summary: Larian Studios' Rivellon RPG series, from the early action-RPGs through Dragon Commander and the turn-based Original Sin games.

entries.title: Divine Divinity

emulation.notes: Run the native PC release with modern compatibility settings if needed.

primary.why: The original Windows release and current PC storefront builds are the practical, highest-fidelity route for Larian's first Divinity RPG. The later OS X port adds access but no exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release through GOG or Steam with compatibility settings if needed.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is documented; use current PC builds for compatibility.

entries.title: Beyond Divinity

emulation.notes: Run the native PC release with modern compatibility settings if needed.

primary.why: Windows is the original and most practical archive route for the Divine Divinity sequel. The later OS X port adds access but no exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release through GOG or Steam with compatibility settings if needed.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is documented; use current PC builds for compatibility.

entries.title: Divinity II
entries.definitive_edition: Divinity II: Developer's Cut on Windows

emulation.notes: Use the native PC Developer's Cut release.

primary.why: Developer's Cut is the final updated version of Divinity II, following Ego Draconis and The Dragon Knight Saga, and Windows gives the best fidelity/capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Divinity II: Developer's Cut on Windows; treat Xbox 360 as a historical console route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Developer's Cut supersedes Ego Draconis/The Dragon Knight Saga for the archive route.

entries.title: Divinity: Dragon Commander

primary.why: Dragon Commander is documented as a Windows release, so the native PC version is the complete and highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release through Steam/GOG with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or port route is documented.

entries.title: Divinity: Original Sin
entries.definitive_edition: Divinity: Original Sin - Enhanced Edition on Windows

primary.why: The Enhanced Edition adds revised story content, full voiceovers, controller support, split-screen co-op, and many gameplay/visual improvements. Windows remains the best fidelity and mod/capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Divinity: Original Sin - Enhanced Edition on Windows through Steam/GOG; choose the original 2014 release only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original save files are not the reason to choose the old release for archive play; Enhanced Edition is the recommended route.

entries.title: Divinity: Original Sin II
entries.definitive_edition: Divinity: Original Sin II - Definitive Edition on Windows

emulation.notes: Use the native PC Definitive Edition.

primary.version: Divinity: Original Sin II - Definitive Edition
primary.why: The Definitive Edition adds content, balance changes, rewritten dialogue, and an overhauled Arena mode, while Windows remains the best fidelity, mod, and capture route. Current-gen console/Switch 2 versions improve console performance but do not add story content.
primary.how_to_play: Play Divinity: Original Sin II - Definitive Edition on Windows through Steam/GOG with current patches; use current-gen console versions only for console capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Current-generation console/Switch 2 releases improve performance and visual output on consoles but do not supersede PC for archive play.
